candidate.blueprint_locator: Management of Care → Case Management/Continuity of Care: coordinate client care with the interprofessional team, facilitate follow-up and referrals, provide discharge/continuity education, communicate changes in client condition, and advocate for client needs.
candidate.blueprint_topic: Management of Care — RN care coordination and longitudinal follow-up in chronic heart failure
candidate.educational_objective: Describe the RN role in multidisciplinary heart-failure follow-up as symptom assessment, self-care and medication education, identification of barriers, and coordination with the interprofessional team without assuming independent prescribing authority.

options.A: Assess symptoms and self-care barriers, reinforce the medication and monitoring plan, and coordinate concerns with the interprofessional team and follow-up services.
options.B: Independently prescribe and titrate all guideline-directed heart-failure medications without an authorized order, protocol, or prescribing authority.
options.C: Limit contact to appointment scheduling because clinical symptom assessment and self-care education are outside the nursing role.
options.D: Wait for the next physician visit before addressing reported worsening symptoms because between-visit care coordination is unnecessary.

candidate.rationale: The AHA/ACC/HFSA guideline supports multidisciplinary heart-failure care, structured self-care education, medication-adherence support, symptom monitoring, and coordinated transitions/follow-up. These functions fit nursing assessment, education, and care coordination. The guideline does not establish universal independent RN prescribing authority, which depends on licensure and local authorization. Therefore, A is the best answer. B overstates scope, while C and D inappropriately exclude nursing clinical assessment and coordination from longitudinal heart-failure care.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Directly supports nursing-compatible roles in symptom/self-care assessment, education, adherence support, and interprofessional coordination during longitudinal heart-failure management while avoiding a universal claim of independent medication-prescribing authority.
candidate.source_document_title: 2022 AHA/ACC/HFSA Guideline for the Management of Heart Failure
candidate.source_locator: Multidisciplinary/self-care recommendations and Section 9.6, Integration of Care: Transitions and Team-Based Approaches: multidisciplinary interventions, case management, coordinated communication, structured self-care education, medication-adherence support, and early postdischarge follow-up improve continuity and are central to HF management. Table 25 includes reinforcing HF education, assessing adherence, safety monitoring, and coordinating follow-up care.
candidate.source_organization: American Heart Association/American College of Cardiology/Heart Failure Society of America
